record.paper_title: XXX Spin Chain: from Bethe Solution to Open Problems
record.original_question: For the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions, compute the correlation functions both in the bulk and at the boundary. The difficulty is that this model lacks translation invariance, although some determinant representations and boundary results are already known near the boundary.

evidence.quote: As in all exactly solvable models the study of correlation functions is of extreme importance. In the case of the six vertex model with DWBC an added difficulty is constituted by the lack of translation invariance.
Open problem: Calculate the bulk and boundary correlation functions of the six vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the six-vertex model on an N×N square lattice with domain wall boundary conditions (DWBC): on each edge place an arrow so that at every internal vertex the ice rule holds (two arrows in, two arrows out), and on the boundary all horizontal arrows on the left and right sides point inward while all vertical arrows on the top and bottom sides point outward (or equivalently, the standard DWBC configuration). Assign Boltzmann weights a, b, c to the six allowed vertex configurations in the usual symmetric way, so that the partition function Z_N(a,b,c) admits the Izergin–Korepin determinant representation.

Define, for a finite collection of lattice edges or vertices, the corresponding (multi-point) correlation function as the weighted statistical average of the indicators of prescribed local arrow/vertex configurations on those edges/vertices, normalized by Z_N.

Problem: Obtain explicit closed-form expressions (e.g. determinant or multiple-integral representations, and their thermodynamic / scaling limits) for the bulk multi-point correlation functions of the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions, as well as for the boundary multi-point correlation functions beyond the already known one-point boundary results. In particular, derive formulas valid uniformly in the disordered, ferroelectric and antiferroelectric phases, taking into account the lack of translation invariance inherent to the DWBC setup.
artifact.category_tag: six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: boundary one-point functions are known as N×N determinants (Bogoliubov–Pronko–Zvonarev), and various nonlocal bulk correlation functions such as the emptiness formation probability and row-configuration probability have been studied by Colomo–Pronko and others, with integral/determinant representations and limit-shape results. However, general bulk and boundary multi-point correlation functions of the DWBC six-vertex model do not have complete closed-form solutions, and the problem is generally considered partially solved / still open.

status_evidence.title: On the problem of calculation of correlation functions in the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of calculation of correlation functions in the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions is addressed by considering a particular nonlocal correlation function, called row configuration probability.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research focuses on specific nonlocal correlation functions rather than a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Boundary correlation functions of the six-vertex model
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary one-point correlation functions are expressed as determinants of N×N matrices, generalizing the known result for the partition function.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary one-point functions are known in determinant form.

status_evidence.title: Six-vertex model on a finite lattice: Integral representations for nonlocal correlation functions
status_evidence.snippet: Integral representations for nonlocal correlation functions in the six-vertex model on a finite lattice with DWBC.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results: integral representations exist for certain nonlocal correlators, but a complete bulk correlation theory remains incomplete.
